terms.gloss: be hidden away for the winter
evidence: Plin. NH 8.132: conduntur hieme et Ponticī mūrēs (M-O s.v. hibernate)
terms.comment: Pliny’s phrase, of animals that lie up for the winter; he also has hībernīs mēnsibus latēre (NH 10.28, in Morgan–Owens). hībernāre means to pass the winter, of troops and ships.

sources: Lewis & Short: condo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. hibernate.
